name: Mica-v0.5-4B
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B: 8 full GQA layers (kv heads 4, head_dim 256) and 24 other layers, per the base config.json.
notes: ADDED 2026-11-07. A DECISION model (task=decision), not a text generator: it takes a state (a log, trace, document or JSON up to 32k tokens) plus typed questions (choice up to 255 options, score up to 255 levels, multi-choice, cannot-grade) and returns a calibrated probability per option from ONE forward pass with ZERO output tokens. Post-trained from Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (catalog record models/qwen3-5-4b), whose geometry it inherits unchanged: 32 layers, 16 query / 4 KV heads, head_dim 256, hidden 2560, 3-linear-then-1-full attention pattern (8 full-attention layers of 32), 262144 native context. The base_model tag is present and the repo's config.json is the stock qwen3_5 text config - the decision readout lives in the head and the trained weights, not in a renamed architecture, so there is no d1-style *_codes key to point at here. PARAMS: HF safetensors total 4,659,865,088 = 4.66B, identical to the base record's 4.66B. active_params_b = params_b (dense). flops_per_token_active = 2 x 4.66e9 = 9.32e9 on the schema's one-pass basis; for a decision model this is the whole inference cost, since no tokens are decoded. KV: 32,768 B/token, inherited from models/qwen3-5-4b - 8 full-attention layers x 2 x 4 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 B = 32,768 B. The 24 linear-attention layers hold a constant state and are excluded; at a 32k-token input that is ~1.07 GiB of KV, which is the reason the card can quote 1.05 s at 32k on one consumer GPU. HARDWARE GATE: passes - 4.66B active, 2.33 GiB at 4-bit against the 128 GiB budget. The card ships INT8 (CUDA runtime), Q8_0 / IQ4_XS / BF16 (llama.cpp) and quotes 15.6 ms per request at 243 median tokens for INT8 on an RTX 6000 Ada, 32.5 ms for IQ4_XS. WHAT IT BEATS: on the card's single Results table - every model's column run by the author under one harness, which the card states explicitly ('Numbers for other models are our runs, not their reported scores') - Mica v0.5 posts JDI 0.3 58.8 vs its own v0.1 at 37.2, a +21.6 point jump on the same suite, and JevBench Hard 84/111, which beats Jev (~100B) 80/111, Solar Decide (35B) 82/111, MS Decision-1 (9B) 91/111 is AHEAD on that one row so the win is not universal, Clef (9B) 72/111 and d1 (3B) 60/111. On the JDI 0.3 column it beats every model its size or smaller and trails only PPLX Decider Flash (60.1, 4B). WHAT IT LOSES: JevBench Hard against MS Decision-1 (9B) 91/111, and against Imajev (4B) 80/111 it wins, so the genuine losses are MS Decision-1 and the JDI 0.3 column against PPLX Decider Flash (60.1) and Jev (~100B, 59.1). SCALE WARNING, DO NOT RANK AGAINST data/decision_index.jsonl: the card's 'JDI 0.3' is the author's own 0.3 suite. The community board the catalog carries (clef-evals mirror of the upstream Space, read 2026-11-07, 73 engines, upstream edition 0.2.1 generated 2026-09-28) has NO row for Mica v0.5 or Mica v0.1 at all, so nothing here is board-measured and the 58.8 is not on the 0.2.1 scale where Clef sits at 61.21. Every row is therefore vendor_claim. BONUS PROPERTY, recorded because a decision readout is judged on it: option order does not move the answer - shuffle the allowed answers and it picks the same one 97.3% of the time (2.7% flip). Author-measured, sample size not printed. LICENCE: apache-2.0, repo created 2026-09-27. Sibling of the already-catalogued models/mica-v0-1-4b, which this record supersedes on every row the two share.

benchmarks.name: JDI 0.3 (Decision Index, author's 0.3 suite)
benchmarks.config: Card 'Results' table, Mica v0.5 column 58.8 vs Mica v0.1 column 37.2 on the same items and scoring (the author ran every model in the column: 'Numbers for other models are our runs, not their reported scores'). NOT the community Decision Index 0.2.1 carried in data/decision_index.jsonl - the card calls it JDI 0.3, so the two are not on one scale. Self-reported by the model author.

benchmarks.name: JevBench Hard (x/111)
benchmarks.config: Same table, Mica v0.5 84/111 vs Mica v0.1 72/111 and vs Jev (~100B) 80/111, Clef (9B) 72/111, Solar Decide (35B) 82/111. Author-reported run of every column under one harness. n=111 single run; no variance printed.

benchmarks.name: Option-order flip rate (lower is better, %)
benchmarks.config: Card prose: 'Shuffle the allowed answers and it picks the same one 97.3% of the time', i.e. 2.7% flip. Recorded because it is the property a decision readout is judged on; higher_is_better is false here and the score field holds the flip rate. Author-measured, sample size not printed.
